files.summary: reconcile delivered custom attribute and value adapters
edits:
The finite `attribute-bindings` authoring kind connects already admitted custom number, reservoir or category definitions to one existing supported body. This is an owner-authorized instance configuration, not a new law, a character's ordinary ability, or an automatic consequence of definition installation. The World Agent obtains its schema from `ol_schema`, inspects definitions and current body state, saves a draft, validates, prepares an exact review, and applies only after the human approves it. MCP and local application callers use the same authoring dispatcher and native mutation owner.
The existing owner body-edit operation is the authority boundary. Attaching an installed definition is not gated as new invention, just as ordinary use of an admitted capability is distinct from defining it. Creating or changing the definition continues to follow the existing invention policy. The broader creator/special-player exception to ordinary invention locks is an accepted target still awaiting INV-1.7/MP02 implementation, as distinguished in [the constitution](world-constitution.md#41-who-can-control-what); this adapter neither implements that grant nor permits NPC access to owner tools.
A separate delivered [custom-value intervention](world-agent-inspection-and-edits.md#reviewed-custom-attribute-values) updates already bound custom attributes through the same native body owner, with exact per-value revisions, human review and permanent Apply receipts. It is not this add-only operation, ordinary replenishment or an untyped property setter. Removal, native-need replacement, sense/controller replacement, bulk species migration and general shared-law replacement remain separate WW10/INV-5 work. INV-21 and WW14 own the delivered value adapter and its remaining qualification; deferred regression cases stay in the maintainer TODO.
